interventions.title: Construct Continuous Sidewalks
interventions.description: Install paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide physical separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Install Curbs and Green Buffers
interventions.description: Define the roadway edge with curbs and add a planting strip to further separate pedestrians from moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Driveway Management
interventions.description: Define specific, narrowed driveway entrances to reduce the width of conflict zones and improve predictability.

interventions.title: Road Diet and Buffer
interventions.description: Reduce lane widths or the number of lanes to provide space for a protected pedestrian buffer or a separated shared-use path.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Resurface the roadway to eliminate cracks and provide a smooth, safe surface for all users.

interventions.title: Walkway Widening
interventions.description: Expand the walkway to a minimum of 5-6 feet to meet standard accessibility requirements.

interventions.title: Emergency Egress Points
interventions.description: Provide designated and signed exit points or refuge areas along the barrier wall.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale and roadway lighting to improve visibility and personal security.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Repair the road surface and narrow the travel lanes to encourage slower vehicle speeds, potentially reclaiming space for a buffered walkway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Install a landscaped buffer or physical barrier between the sidewalk and the roadway to protect pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island to facilitate safe crossing of the wide roadway.

interventions.title: Install Paved Sidewalks
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on at least one side of the street to provide safe pedestrian passage.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Exclusion and Signage
interventions.description: If this is a high-speed facility, clear signage should prohibit pedestrian access and provide information on alternative safe routes.

interventions.title: Separated Pedestrian Facility
interventions.description: If pedestrian access is required, a fully grade-separated walkway or a wide, barrier-protected sidewalk should be constructed.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Enhancements
interventions.description: Improve lighting levels to increase pedestrian visibility and security in this industrial area.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to slow vehicle speeds and create space for a protected pedestrian or bicycle facility.

interventions.title: Debris Removal and Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Clear the shoulder of trash and repair the cracked pavement to improve walking conditions in the short term.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to encourage lower vehicle speeds and reclaim space for a dedicated pedestrian or bicycle facility.

interventions.title: Install Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip, bollards, or a furniture zone to provide physical and psychological separation from moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Installation
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Prohibit Pedestrian Access
interventions.description: If this is a limited-access highway, ensure clear signage and physical barriers prevent pedestrian entry.

interventions.title: Construct Separated Pedestrian Path
interventions.description: If pedestrian access is required, a physically separated and protected walkway must be constructed behind the barrier or on a separate grade.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Buffer
interventions.description: Widen the existing narrow sidewalk on the right and add a planting strip or furniture zone to buffer pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: Roadway and Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Repave the street and sidewalk to eliminate trip hazards and improve accessibility for all users.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a standard-width sidewalk on the right side of the roadway to provide a continuous path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Install Separated Sidewalk
interventions.description: Construct a paved sidewalk with physical separation from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Add Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install luminaires to provide visibility and security for the pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: Enhanced Street Lighting
interventions.description: Improve illumination specifically for the pedestrian realm to increase visibility and safety during low-light conditions.

interventions.title: Roadway and Sidewalk Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked and failing pavement on both the roadway and the walkway to eliminate trip hazards and improve accessibility.

interventions.title: Clear Sidewalk Obstructions
interventions.description: Enforce regulations to keep the sidewalk clear of industrial equipment and dumpsters to maintain a continuous walking path.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Install speed humps or narrowing treatments to reduce vehicle speeds in this constrained industrial corridor.

interventions.title: Construct a separated sidewalk
interventions.description: Provide a paved, ADA-compliant walkway separated from the roadway by a buffer or the existing barriers if space allows.

interventions.title: Install street lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting to improve visibility and personal security along the wall.
